links.outcome: Physician-rated completeness and accuracy of AI-generated hospital course narratives versus clinician-authored
links.effect: AI lower for completeness (-0.84; 95% CI, -1.36 to -0.32; adjusted p=0.012) and accuracy (-0.35; 95% CI, -0.66 to -0.05); only completeness significant after Bonferroni correction.
links.quote: AI-generated narratives were rated higher for clarity (0.36; 95% CI, 0.07 to 0.65) and readability (0.72; 95% CI, 0.20 to 1.24) but lower for completeness (-0.84; 95% CI, -1.36 to -0.32) and accuracy (-0.35; 95% CI, -0.66 to -0.05).

links.outcome: Physician-rated overall quality and preference, AI versus clinician-authored narratives, blinded paired comparison
links.effect: Overall quality did not differ (7.27 AI vs 7.42 clinician; difference -0.15; p=0.627); clinician preferred in 52.8% vs AI 47.2% (OR 1.12; 95% CI 0.71 to 1.78).
links.quote: Overall quality did not differ significantly (mean, 7.27 AI-generated versus 7.42 clinician-authored; difference, -0.15; 95% CI, -0.86 to 0.56; p=0.627).

unlisted_practices: Agentic EHR-integrated retrieval via Model Context Protocol tools to reduce omissions in discharge narrative generation

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of an agentic LLM system for drafting hospital course narratives compared with clinician-authored notes using physician ratings; does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
